questions.prompt: Do you usually carry an umbrella with you?

No. I no have umbrella.

Rain, no good.

Well, usually I don't carry an umbrella.

I only take it if I think it's going to rain.

For example, if the weather forecast says it will rain, then I will bring it.

However, sometimes I forget to check the weather, so I don't have one.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I don't usually bother carrying one, though I probably should. I tend to check the weather app before I head out, and if rain's on the cards, I'll chuck a foldable umbrella in my bag. Otherwise I just take my chances — and yeah, I've been caught out in a downpour more than once.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Ba'zida men soyabon olib yuraman.

Agar yomg'ir bo'lsa, men soyabonni olaman.

Lekin ba'zida uni uyda unutib qoldiraman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, odatda men soyabon olib yurmayman.

Men uni faqat yomg'ir yog'adi deb o'ylasam olaman.

Masalan, agar ob-havo bashorati yomg'ir yog'ishini aytsa, unda men uni olib boraman.

Biroq, ba'zida ob-havoni tekshirishni unutib qo'yaman, shuning uchun menda soyabon bo'lmaydi.

Men odatda soyabon olib yurmayman, lekin ehtimol olib yurishim kerakdir.

Biroq, agar ob-havo noaniq bo'lsa, ko'pincha tavakkal qilib, uni tashlab ketaman, bu har doim ham eng yaxshi qaror emas, chunki men bir necha marta kutilmagan yomg'irga tushib qolganman.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Do you usually carry an umbrella with you?
idioms: save it for a rainy day - "og'ir kunga asramoq"
come rain or shine - "qanday bo'lmasin, har qanday holatda"
sentenceStarters: "To be honest, I don't always…" - "Rostini aytsam, men har doim…emasman"
"I tend to check the weather…" - "Men ob-havoni tekshirishga odatlanganman…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
To be honest, I don't always carry an umbrella, although I probably should. I tend to check the weather forecast on my phone before leaving the house, and if rain is expected, I'll grab a small foldable umbrella.
That said, I've been caught in the rain without one more times than I'd like to admit, so I'm trying to make it a habit to keep one in my bag.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, men doim soyabon olib yurmayman, garchi olib yurishim kerak bo'lsa ham kerak. Uyimdan chiqishdan oldin telefonimda ob-havo ma'lumotlarini tekshirishga harakat qilaman va agar yomg'ir yog'ishi kutilsa, kichik buklanadigan soyabonni olaman.

Shunga qaramay, men xohlaganimdan ko'ra ko'proq marta soyabonsiz yomg'irda qolganman, shuning uchun men sumkamda doim soyabon saqlashni odat qilishga harakat qilyapman.

Bu mening tajribalarimni hujjatlashtirishning ajoyib usuli va men ularni do'stlarim va oilam bilan baham ko'rishni ham yoqtiraman. O'ylashimcha, bu xotiralarni saqlab qolishning bir usuli.

Yes, I really enjoy taking photographs, especially when I'm travelling or spending time outdoors. I find it's a wonderful way to capture memories and appreciate the beauty around me.
I mostly use my smartphone camera, which is surprisingly good these days. I wouldn't call myself a professional, but I do like experimenting with different angles and lighting.

Ha, men suratga olishni juda yoqtiraman, ayniqsa sayohat qilganimda yoki tabiatda vaqt o'tkazganimda. Menimcha, bu xotiralarni saqlab qolish va atrofimdagi go'zallikni qadrlashning ajoyib usuli.

Men asosan smartfon kameramdan foydalanaman, u hozirgi kunda hayratlanarli darajada yaxshi. Men o'zimni professional deb atay olmayman, lekin turli burchaklar va yorug'lik bilan tajriba o'tkazishni yaxshi ko'raman.

questions.prompt: Are you good at remembering people's names?
questions.sampleA1: No. I am not good. Names are hard.
questions.sampleA2: No, I am not very good at remembering names. It is difficult for me. I forget them quickly, but I try to remember.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I'm not terrible at remembering names, but I'm not great either. I usually remember faces better. I think it's because I don't always pay attention when someone says their name the first time. However, I try to repeat their name when I meet them to help me remember.
questions.sampleB2: Honestly, not really — it's something I've always struggled with. I'm much better with faces; a name just goes in one ear and out the other. The thing is, I often don't pay enough attention the first time round. These days I try to repeat the name straight away and link it to something memorable.
questions.uzSampleA2: Yo'q, men odamlarning ismlarini eslab qolishda unchalik yaxshi emasman. Bu men uchun qiyin. Men ularni tezda unutib qo'yaman, lekin eslab qolishga harakat qilaman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, ismlarni eslab qolishda juda yomon emasman, lekin a'lo ham emasman. Odatda yuzlarni yaxshiroq eslayman. Menimcha, buning sababi, kimdir birinchi marta ismini aytganda, har doim ham e'tibor bermayman.
Shunga qaramay, eslab qolishimga yordam berish uchun, kim bilan uchrashsam, ismini takrorlashga harakat qilaman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men ismlarni eslab qolish uchun tabiiy iste'dodim bor deb ayta olmayman; bu ustida faol ishlashim kerak bo'lgan narsa. Ko'pincha, ayniqsa katta guruhlarda, tanishtiruvlardan keyin hamma ismini eslab qolishda qiynalaman. Buni qoplash uchun men ismni ajratib turadigan xususiyat bilan bog'lashga yoki suhbatda takrorlashga ongli ravishda harakat qilaman. Bu strategiya mukammal bo'lmasa-da, u mening eslash darajamni aniq yaxshilaydi, garchi men ba'zida kimningdir ismini aytganidan keyin darhol unutib, noqulay vaziyatga tushib qolaman.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Are you good at remembering people's names?
idioms: it's on the tip of my tongue - "tilimning uchida turibdi"
sentenceStarters: "I have to admit, I'm not particularly…" - "Tan olishim kerak, men unchalik…emasman"
"I've been trying to improve by…" - "Men …orqali yaxshilashga harakat qilyapman"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I have to admit, I'm not particularly good at remembering names, which can be quite embarrassing at times. I often find myself in situations where I recognise someone's face but draw a complete blank on their name.
I've been trying to improve by repeating the name when I first meet someone and associating it with something memorable. It's a work in progress, though.

Tan olishim kerak, men ismlarni eslab qolishda unchalik yaxshi emasman, bu ba'zan juda noqulay vaziyatlarni keltirib chiqarishi mumkin. Ko'pincha kimningdir yuzini tanisam ham, ismini umuman eslay olmaydigan vaziyatlarga tushib qolaman.

Yaxshilashga harakat qilyapman, birinchi marta kim bilandir uchrashganimda ismini takrorlayman va uni esda qolarli biror narsa bilan bog'layman. Lekin bu hali jarayon.

Ikkinchi rasmda esa, kimdir landshaftning tezkor suratini olish uchun smartfonni beparvo ushlab turibdi. Bu ikki rasm o'rtasidagi asosiy farq - bu jihozlar darajasi va jalb qilingan sadoqat — biri professional fotografiyani ifodalasa, ikkinchisi kundalik oddiy suratga olishni ko'rsatadi.

questions.prompt: What are the benefits of using a professional camera?
questions.sampleA2: A good camera is good. It takes better pictures and the pictures are more clear. I like good pictures and I want a better camera because my phone is not good.
questions.sampleB1: I think a professional camera is better than my phone. For example, the pictures are more clear. Also, you can change the lenses. I think that's good because you can take different types of photos. However, they are very expensive.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the biggest benefit has to be the image quality — professional cameras have far bigger sensors, so they pick up loads more detail and cope much better in low light. On top of that, you get full manual control and interchangeable lenses, which gives you real creative freedom to shoot anything from sweeping landscapes to sharp portraits.
questions.uzSampleA2: Yaxshi kamera yaxshi. U yaxshiroq rasmlar oladi va rasmlar aniqroq bo'ladi. Menga yaxshi rasmlar yoqadi va men yaxshiroq kamera xohlayman, chunki mening telefonim yaxshi emas.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, professional kamera telefonimdan yaxshiroq.
Misol uchun, rasmlar aniqroq. Shuningdek, linzalarni almashtirish mumkin. Menimcha, bu yaxshi, chunki turli xil fotosuratlar olishingiz mumkin.
Biroq, ular juda qimmat.
questions.uzSampleB2: Xo'sh, menimcha professional kameraning asosiy afzalligi uning yuqori sifatli tasvirlarida. Siz ancha ko'p detal olasiz va murakkab yorug'lik sharoitlarida yaxshiroq ishlashga erishasiz. Bundan tashqari, qo'lda sozlashlar va turli xil linzalardan foydalanish imkoniyati tufayli yakuniy tasvir ustidan ko'proq nazoratga ega bo'lasiz. Bu esa ancha ko'proq ijodiy ifoda va haqiqatan ham hayratlanarli fotosuratlarni olish imkoniyatini beradi.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the benefits of using a professional camera?
idioms: a craftsman is only as good as his tools - "usta asboblariga qarab baholanadi"
the devil is in the detail - "muvaffaqiyat tafsilotlarda"
sentenceStarters: "There are numerous benefits to…" - "…ning ko'plab afzalliklari bor…"
"First and foremost, the image quality…" - "Eng avvalo, rasm sifati…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are numerous benefits to using a professional camera. First and foremost, the image quality is vastly superior — professional cameras have larger sensors that capture more detail, richer colours, and perform significantly better in low-light conditions.
They also offer manual controls over settings like aperture, shutter speed, and ISO, giving the photographer complete creative freedom. Another major advantage is the range of interchangeable lenses available, which allow you to shoot everything from wide-angle landscapes to close-up portraits with stunning depth of field.
For anyone pursuing photography as a career or a serious hobby, a professional camera is undoubtedly a worthwhile investment. As they say, "a craftsman is only as good as his tools", and having the right equipment makes all the difference.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Professional kamera ishlatishning ko'plab afzalliklari bor. Birinchi navbatda, tasvir sifati ancha yuqori — professional kameralar kattaroq sensorlarga ega bo'lib, ular ko'proq detallarni, boyroq ranglarni qamrab oladi va kam yorug'lik sharoitida sezilarli darajada yaxshiroq ishlaydi.

Ular, shuningdek, diafragma, tortishish tezligi va ISO kabi sozlamalar ustidan qo'lda boshqaruvni taklif qiladi, bu esa fotograflarga to'liq ijodiy erkinlik beradi. Yana bir asosiy afzalligi - almashtiriladigan linzalarning mavjudligi bo'lib, ular yordamida siz keng burchakli landshaftlardan tortib, ajoyib chuqurlikka ega yaqin portretlargacha hamma narsani suratga olishingiz mumkin.

Agar kimdir fotografiyani kasb yoki jiddiy mashg'ulot sifatida davom ettirmoqchi bo'lsa, professional kamera, shubhasiz, arzirli sarmoyadir. Aytishlaricha, "hunarmand faqat o'z asboblari kabi yaxshi" va to'g'ri jihozga ega bo'lish katta ahamiyatga ega.

questions.prompt: Why do most people rely on smartphones for photography today?
questions.sampleA1: I have a phone. I take pictures with my phone. It's easy.
questions.sampleA2: I use my phone for photos. It's easy to carry and it's always with me. And the photos are okay. I don't need a camera.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think most people use smartphones because it's very convenient. You always have your phone with you. Also, the cameras on phones are pretty good now. For example, my phone takes really nice pictures. So, I don't need a separate camera.
questions.sampleB2: Well, honestly, it mostly comes down to sheer convenience. Nearly everyone carries a phone around all day, so it's always on hand to capture a moment. The cameras have got remarkably good too, and there's no faffing about with settings — you just point and shoot. Best of all, you can share the photo online within seconds.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menda telefon bor. Men telefonim bilan suratga olaman. Bu oson.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men suratlar uchun telefonimdan foydalanaman. Uni olib yurish oson va u doim men bilan birga. Va suratlar yaxshi. Menga kamera kerak emas.
questions.uzSampleB1: Xo'sh, menimcha, ko'pchilik smartfonlardan foydalanadi, chunki bu juda qulay. Telefoningiz har doim siz bilan birga bo'ladi. Bundan tashqari, telefonlardagi kameralar hozir juda yaxshi. Masalan, mening telefonim juda chiroyli suratlar oladi. Shuning uchun, menga alohida kamera kerak emas.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Menimcha, odamlarning fotosuratga olish uchun smartfonlarga keng tayanishi, asosan, ularning qulayligi va foydalanish osonligidan kelib chiqadi. Deyarli har kimda smartfon bor, bu esa uni lahzalarni suratga olish uchun oson vositaga aylantiradi. Bundan tashqari, tasvir sifati keskin yaxshilandi, ko'pincha maxsus kameralar sifatiga teng keladi, ayniqsa kundalik suratlar va ijtimoiy tarmoqlar uchun mo'ljallangan kontent uchun.

Yana bir muhim omil - ijtimoiy media platformalari bilan uzluksiz integratsiya. Smartfon bilan olingan fotosuratlarni baham ko'rish oson, bu ko'plab foydalanuvchilar uchun katta afzallikdir.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why do most people rely on smartphones for photography today?
idioms: the best camera is the one you have with you - "eng yaxshi kamera — doim yoningdagisi"
sentenceStarters: "The main reason most people rely on…" - "Ko'pchilik …ga tayanishining asosiy sababi…"
"Unlike professional cameras, smartphones…" - "Professional kameralardan farqli, smartfonlar…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
The main reason most people rely on smartphones for photography is sheer convenience. Almost everyone carries a phone with them at all times, so it's always ready to capture a spontaneous moment.
Modern smartphone cameras have also become remarkably advanced, producing high-quality images that are more than sufficient for everyday use and social media sharing. Unlike professional cameras, smartphones don't require any technical knowledge — you simply point and shoot, and built-in software automatically adjusts the settings for you.
There's also the instant sharing factor: people can take a photo and post it online within seconds, which appeals to our desire for immediate gratification. As the saying goes, "the best camera is the one you have with you", and for most people, that's their smartphone.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ko'pchilikning bugungi kunda suratga olish uchun smartfonlarga tayanishining asosiy sababi – bu juda qulaylik.

Zamonaviy smartfon kameralari ham juda rivojlanib ketgan, kundalik foydalanish va ijtimoiy tarmoqlarda baham ko'rish uchun yetarli bo'lgan yuqori sifatli tasvirlarni yaratadi. Professional kameralardan farqli o'laroq, smartfonlar hech qanday texnik bilimlarni talab qilmaydi – siz shunchaki nishonga olasiz va suratga olasiz, o'rnatilgan dasturiy ta'minot esa sozlamalarni avtomatik ravishda sozlaydi.

Shuningdek, tezkor baham ko'rish omili ham bor: odamlar suratga olib, uni bir necha soniya ichida onlayn joylashtirishlari mumkin, bu esa bizning zudlik bilan qoniqish istagimizga mos keladi. Aytganlaridek, "eng yaxshi kamera - bu siz bilan birga bo'lgan kamera", ko'pchilik uchun esa bu ularning smartfoni.

questions.prompt: Describe a time you had to wait a long time for something or someone.
questions.sampleA1: I wait for bus. Bus is late. I am sad.
questions.sampleA2: I waited for my birthday. It was a long time. I wanted presents and cake. I was happy when it came.
questions.sampleB1: I remember waiting for a new phone. I ordered it online, and it took two weeks to arrive. I was really excited, so it felt like a very long time. I was checking the tracking information every day. Finally, it arrived, and I was very happy, but the waiting was difficult.
questions.sampleB2: Right, I'd like to talk about a time when I had to wait ages for the results of a big university entrance exam. Honestly, that waiting period was absolutely nerve-wracking, because my whole future seemed to hinge on that one result. I remember refreshing my email and the university website dozens of times a day, hoping something would finally turn up. Weeks dragged on, and each day felt like it lasted forever. Looking back, though, that experience did wonders for my patience — in a roundabout way. It taught me that some things are simply beyond my control, and that stewing over them doesn't change the outcome one bit. So instead of sitting around fretting, I learned to channel my energy into more productive things, like lining up a backup plan in case it didn't go my way. On the whole, I'd say it made me a far more resilient person. As for why people nowadays find it so hard to wait, I reckon it boils down to the culture of instant gratification that technology has created. We're used to getting answers online in the blink of an eye, having parcels delivered the same day, and streaming whatever we fancy on demand. All of that has gradually chipped away at our patience and shortened our attention spans. The thing is, real life doesn't always work at that pace, so when we're forced to wait, it feels far more frustrating than it probably should. Patience, as they say, is a virtue — but it's one that's getting harder and harder to hold on to these days.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men avtobusni kutdim. Avtobus kech qoldi. Men xafa bo'ldim.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men tug'ilgan kunimni kutdim. Bu uzoq vaqt edi. Men sovg'alar va tort xohlardim. U kelganida men xursand bo'ldim.
questions.uzSampleB1: Esimda, men yangi telefon kutgan edim. Men uni internetdan buyurtma bergan edim va u ikki hafta ichida keldi. Men juda xursand edim, shuning uchun u juda uzoq vaqtga o'xshab tuyuldi. Men har kuni kuzatuv ma'lumotlarini tekshirib turardim. Nihoyat, u keldi va men juda xursand bo'ldim, lekin kutish qiyin edi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Esimda, chet elga sayohat qilish uchun viza olishni kutish bilan bog'liq ayniqsa asabiylashuvchi holat bo'lgan. Ariza topshirish jarayoni juda uzoq edi va ko'rib chiqish vaqtlari oldindan aytib bo'lmaydigan edi. Haftalar oylarga aylandi va men doimiy ravishda elchixonaning veb-saytini yangiliklar uchun tekshirib turardim. Hech qanday aniq reja tuzish qiyin edi, chunki qachon yoki hatto viza olamanmi yoki yo'qmi bilmasdim. Bu tajriba menga sabrning muhimligi va muayyan vaziyatlar ustidan nazorat qilish imkoniyatlarimning cheklanganligi haqida ko'p narsalarni o'rgatdi.

vocabulary.title: Q7 - Describe a time you had to wait a long time for something or someone

bulletPoints: Describe a time you had to wait a long time for something or someone.
How did this experience affect your patience?
Why do people in modern society often find it difficult to wait?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A time I had to wait:
I'd like to talk about a time when I had to wait for several months to receive the results of a university entrance exam. The waiting period was incredibly stressful because my entire future depended on that outcome, and every day felt like an eternity. I remember constantly checking my email and the university website, hoping for any update.
How it affected my patience:
This experience significantly affected my patience — in a positive way, actually. It taught me that some things are simply beyond our control, and worrying excessively doesn't change the outcome. I learned to channel my energy into productive activities while waiting, such as preparing for alternative plans. It made me a more resilient person overall.
Why people find it difficult to wait:
As for why people in modern society find it difficult to wait, I believe it's largely due to the culture of instant gratification that technology has created. We're used to getting answers from the internet in seconds, receiving same-day deliveries, and streaming content on demand. This has dramatically shortened our attention spans and made us less tolerant of delays.

Men universitetga kirish imtihonlari natijalarini olish uchun bir necha oy kutishga to'g'ri kelgan vaqt haqida gapirmoqchiman. Kutish davri juda stressli edi, chunki butun kelajagim shu natijaga bog'liq edi va har bir kun abadiyatdek tuyulardi. Bu mening sabrimga qanday ta'sir qildi:

Bu tajriba mening sabrimga sezilarli ta'sir ko'rsatdi — aslida ijobiy tomonga. Bu menga ba'zi narsalar shunchaki bizning nazoratimizdan tashqarida ekanligini va haddan tashqari tashvishlanish natijani o'zgartirmasligini o'rgatdi. Kutish davomida energiyamni muqobil rejalarga tayyorgarlik ko'rish kabi samarali faoliyatlarga yo'naltirishni o'rgandim. Bu meni umuman olganda yanada chidamli insonga aylantirdi.

Nima uchun odamlar kutishni qiyin deb bilishadi:

Nima uchun zamonaviy jamiyatda odamlar kutishni qiyin deb bilishlariga kelsak, menimcha, buning asosiy sababi texnologiya yaratgan tezkor qoniqish madaniyatidir. Bu bizning diqqatimizni keskin qisqartirdi va kechikishlarga nisbatan kamroq bardoshli qildi.

questions.prompt: Public transportation should be completely free for everyone.
questions.sampleA1: Bus free? Yes, good. I like bus. I go shop.
questions.sampleA2: Free bus is good, I think. Because I don't have car. And it's cheaper for me. But maybe it's bad because many people use bus.
questions.sampleB1: I think free public transport is a good idea. It would help people who don't have much money. Also, it could reduce the amount of cars on the road, which is good for the environment. However, I'm not sure if it's realistic. Where will the money come from?
questions.sampleB2: This is a really topical debate these days, especially with cities getting more and more congested. On the one hand, supporters of free public transport make some compelling points. It would give equal mobility to lower-income people who simply can't afford a car, which goes a long way towards levelling the playing field. It would also cut down on traffic congestion and air pollution, since more people would be tempted to leave their cars at home and hop on a bus or train instead. On the other hand, the critics do have a point. Scrapping fares altogether would place a massive financial burden on the government, and that money would have to come from somewhere — most likely higher taxes. There's also a genuine worry that without ticket revenue, the quality, safety, and upkeep of the whole system might gradually go downhill. On top of that, free services tend to get seriously overcrowded during rush hour, which could put people off using them. Personally, I'm sitting on the fence a little. I can genuinely see the appeal of it, but I lean towards a more balanced approach — say, heavily subsidised fares for students and pensioners rather than making everything free across the board. That way you keep it affordable without breaking the bank. After all, if the service ends up unreliable and packed, nobody really benefits in the long run. At the end of the day, as the saying goes, there's no such thing as a free lunch, so someone, somewhere, always ends up footing the bill.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a particularly relevant debate in today's urban landscape. Supporters of free public transport argue that it provides equal mobility for low-income citizens who cannot afford cars, thereby promoting social equality. They also point out that free transit would significantly reduce traffic congestion and air pollution in major cities, as more people would be encouraged to leave their personal vehicles at home.
On the other hand, critics raise some valid concerns. Making public transport entirely free would create a massive financial burden on governments, which would inevitably need to be covered through higher taxes. There's also the worry that without ticket revenue, the quality, safety, and maintenance of transport systems could gradually decline. Additionally, completely free services often lead to severe overcrowding during peak hours.
In my opinion, a more balanced approach — such as heavily subsidised fares rather than completely free transport — might be the best solution. As the saying goes, "there's no such thing as a free lunch", and someone always has to foot the bill.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu bugungi shahar manzarasida ayniqsa dolzarb bahsdir. Bepul jamoat transportini qo'llab-quvvatlovchilar uning avtomobil sotib olishga qurbi yetmaydigan kam daromadli fuqarolar uchun teng harakatlanish imkoniyatini ta'minlashini, shu bilan ijtimoiy tenglikni rag'batlantirishini ta'kidlaydilar. Ular, shuningdek, bepul tranzit yirik shaharlarda tirbandlik va havo ifloslanishini sezilarli darajada kamaytiradi, chunki ko'proq odamlar shaxsiy transport vositalarini uyda qoldirishga undaladi, deb ta'kidlaydilar.

Boshqa tomondan, tanqidchilar ba'zi asosli xavotirlarni o'rtaga tashlaydilar. Jamoat transportini butunlay bepul qilish hukumatlar uchun katta moliyaviy yuk yaratadi, uni, albatta, yuqori soliqlar orqali qoplash kerak bo'ladi. Shuningdek, chipta daromadi bo'lmasa, transport tizimlarining sifati, xavfsizligi va ta'minoti asta-sekin yomonlashishi mumkin degan xavotir ham bor. Bundan tashqari, butunlay bepul xizmatlar ko'pincha eng gavjum soatlarda haddan tashqari olomon bo'lishiga olib keladi.

Mening fikrimcha, butunlay bepul transportdan ko'ra, arzonlashtirilgan narxlar kabi yanada muvozanatli yondashuv eng yaxshi yechim bo'lishi mumkin. Aytganlaridek, "tekin pishloq faqat qopqonda bo'ladi", va har doim kimdir to'lashi kerak.
